rationale: The exposure is recorded for every discharge on the scanned template, and 90-day revisits are common enough (about one child in six) that following all discharges is efficient. A cohort keeps the timing of plan and revisit clear and lets the analysis adjust for the confounders named in the retrieved methods review (c5). Linkage to the provincial dataset is required because a fifth of revisits happen elsewhere (c2). Reporting follows STROBE with the RECORD extension.
alternatives: Chart-based analysis of revisits to this hospital only (refused: misses about one revisit in five, unequally by income)
Case-control study of children who revisited (refused: the outcome is not rare and exposure timing is clearer in a cohort)
Randomised comparison of an electronic plan against the paper plan (deferred: justified only if completeness shows a meaningful association)
whyNotMoreComplex: A trial of the electronic plan would answer the funding question directly but needs money and a signal worth testing; the cohort uses existing charts and linked data to decide whether that signal exists.

decision.statement: Pursue a cohort of first asthma discharges from 2022 to 2025 with plan completeness scored by the five-item score and 90-day revisits from the provincial emergency visits dataset, adjusted for the pre-specified severity and engagement set, because a comparable cohort found an association (c1), a fifth of revisits happen elsewhere (c2), the score is reliable (c3) and confounding by severity is the main threat (c5).
decision.question: Should the pathway team run a linked cohort of plan completeness and 90-day emergency revisits before funding an electronic plan?

criteria.text: A complete plan has been associated with fewer revisits elsewhere, and revisits can be counted across hospitals with linkage.
A provincial analysis of plan completeness and revisits already covers this hospital's discharges.

gates.requirement: Research ethics board approval with a waiver of consent for secondary use of charts
gates.evidence: REB approval REB-2026-0871 dated 2026-09-02, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Signed data sharing agreement with the provincial emergency visits data custodian
gates.evidence: The custodian returned the draft agreement unsigned on 2026-09-09 and asked for a revised privacy impact assessment (investigator local fact)

alternatives: Chart-based analysis of revisits to this hospital only
Improvement project on plan completion without an outcome comparison
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1, c2, c3 and c5 from retrieved records. The ethics gate is met on the investigator's approval record; the data sharing gate is unmet, so the action stays blocked until the agreement is signed.

summary: Cohort recommended; the decision rests on four ledger claims, the ethics gate is met and the data sharing gate is unmet.
